title: Bridge Failure Mode Atlas
purpose: Classify bridge-specific risks including false unification, category confusion, physical escalation, projection identity error, and loss-differential overreading.

failure_mode_classes.name: false_unification
failure_mode_classes.definition: Bridge comparison is misread as proof that QM-like and GR-like domains are unified.

failure_mode_classes.name: category_confusion
failure_mode_classes.definition: Projection analogs are confused with physical quantum mechanics or general relativity.

failure_mode_classes.name: projection_identity_error
failure_mode_classes.definition: Shared source traceability is mistaken for identity between projections.

failure_mode_classes.name: loss_differential_overreading
failure_mode_classes.definition: Different projection losses are interpreted as physical complementarity or explanatory proof.

failure_mode_classes.name: conflict_erasure
failure_mode_classes.definition: Discrete/smooth or threshold/flow conflicts are erased rather than recorded.

failure_mode_classes.name: source_reconstruction_overclaim
failure_mode_classes.definition: Bridge comparison is claimed to reconstruct the whole ⇔R source relation.

failure_mode_classes.name: physical_law_escalation
failure_mode_classes.definition: Bridge artifacts are used to claim derivation of physical laws.

mitigation_rules.rule: Any unification language must be replaced with bridge-analog comparison language.
Any physical interpretation must be rejected unless separately governed outside this phase.
Shared traceability must be restated as non-identity.
Projection conflicts must be restored when erased.
Loss differentials must be treated as analog-only comparison structure.

forbidden_uses: Using bridge failure modes as proof of unification.
Treating category confusion as productive ambiguity.
Promoting loss differential into physical complementarity.
Using shared source traceability as source reconstruction.
Removing conflict records to simplify bridge results.
